title: Type Ia supernova Hubble diagram: Pantheon+SH0ES, 1,701 light curves

object.name: Type Ia supernovae of the Pantheon+ compilation (1,701 light curves of 1,543 distinct supernovae) with the SH0ES Cepheid calibrators
object.frame: redshift in the CMB frame; distance modulus on the SH0ES-calibrated scale

facility.observatory: Surveys and samples (SDSS, SNLS, CSP, DES, Pan-STARRS, CfA, LOSS, HST and others), compiled by the Pantheon+ team

credit: Scolnic et al. 2022 (ApJ 938, 113), Brout et al. 2022 (ApJ 938, 110), Riess et al. 2022 (ApJL 934, L7): the Pantheon+SH0ES data release, cited paper by paper as its release page asks

license.statement: The release page (https://pantheonplussh0es.github.io/, read 2026-10-11) states no licence and says only "Please cite papers individually when referencing them." and that "Details on data release usage will be added upon journal acceptance"; the data repository (https://github.com/PantheonPlusSH0ES/DataRelease, commit 7fc6805) carries no LICENSE file and its READMEs state no terms of use. The table is public.
license.basis: Shipped on the data-pack "no licence stated, credited" basis with the citations the release page requests, by Carl's instruction of 2026-10-11 (DECISION_REGISTER.md D-RIGHTS-04), the basis of D-SKY-02.

columns.name: redshift
columns.description: zHD, the Hubble-diagram redshift (CMB frame, corrected for peculiar velocity)

columns.name: distance modulus
columns.description: MU_SH0ES, on the release's scale: the supernova absolute magnitude fixed from the SH0ES Cepheid host distances (H0 near 73)

columns.name: distance modulus error
columns.description: MU_SH0ES_ERR_DIAG, the diagonal of the full covariance: for plotting only, the release's own warning

columns.name: Cepheid calibrator
columns.description: IS_CALIBRATOR: 1 for a supernova in a host with a Cepheid distance (the release's calibrators), 0 otherwise

columns.name: survey code
columns.description: IDSURVEY, the release's survey number (1 SDSS, 4 SNLS, 5 CSP, 10 DES, 15 PS1MD, 50 to 65 low-redshift samples, 100 to 106 HST, 150 FOUND)

reductions: All 1,701 rows of Pantheon+SH0ES.dat (commit 7fc6805), sorted by redshift, then identifier, then survey code. A supernova observed by two surveys is two rows, as the release has it. Of the 47 columns, five are kept and the identifier is not; the other 41 columns (SALT2 parameters, host properties, positions, bias corrections) are left out.

Errors are the diagonal of the full statistical-plus-systematic covariance, which the release says is for plotting only. The 33 MB covariance is not shipped, so a fit to this table is not the published fit and its Omega_m carries a larger scatter than the published error.
The distance moduli sit on the SH0ES-calibrated scale, so H0 is not measured by the supernovae alone: they fix the shape of the curve, not its scale. 77 rows are Cepheid calibrators.

111 of the 1,701 rows have z below 0.01, where peculiar velocities dominate; the release keeps them and so does this table. Redshift is stored to 1e-5, the modulus to 1e-4 mag and its error to 1e-6, the raw file's digits: the stored table's mean redshift and mean modulus equal the raw file's to better than 1e-12 relative.

source.archive: Pantheon+SH0ES data release on GitHub (PantheonPlusSH0ES/DataRelease), file Pantheon+_Data/4_DISTANCES_AND_COVAR/Pantheon+SH0ES.dat

citations.text: Scolnic et al. 2022, ApJ 938, 113 (The Pantheon+ Analysis: The Full Data Set and Light-curve Release)
Brout et al. 2022, ApJ 938, 110 (The Pantheon+ Analysis: Cosmological Constraints)
Riess et al. 2022, ApJL 934, L7 (A Comprehensive Measurement of the Local Value of the Hubble Constant with 1 km/s/Mpc Uncertainty from the Hubble Space Telescope and the SH0ES Team)

steps: Read zHD, MU_SH0ES, MU_SH0ES_ERR_DIAG, IS_CALIBRATOR and IDSURVEY from Pantheon+SH0ES.dat (whitespace-separated, as the release holds it).
Sort by zHD, then by identifier, then by survey code.
Store redshift, modulus, error, calibrator flag and survey code as table-columns/1.

assumptions: The errors are the covariance diagonal and treat the points as independent, which they are not (shared calibration and a common absolute-magnitude zero point); a lesson must say so.
The raw file is committed beside this tool (tools/data-packs/cosmology/Pantheon+SH0ES.dat, 579,283 bytes) at the commit named in its URL, so the build does not depend on a repository that may change.

validation.check: a flat Lambda-CDM fit with the offset solved gives Omega_m within 0.08 of the published flat value 0.334 +- 0.018 (covariance diagonal only here, the full covariance there)
